sense: go firm, of a jelly, a custard, or a filling

terms.gloss: thicken, set, go firm (of a liquid)
evidence: Verg. G. 3.360: concrēscunt subitae currentī in flūmine crustae
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “generally of soft or liquid substances which thicken; to harden, condense, curdle, stiffen, congeal”. Columella uses it of milk setting into curd, and it serves as well for a jelly, a custard, or a cheesecake filling that firms up in the fridge. Its participle gives Traupman’s sorbillum concrētum, jelly (see “jello”).

terms.gloss: come together, set (of milk with rennet)
evidence: Varr. RR 2.11: addunt coāgulum … ut coeat

phrases.english: Let it set in the fridge.
Has it set yet? — Not yet; it’s still wobbly.

phrases.latin: et cōnfestim cum concrēvit liquor, in fiscellās aut in calathōs vel fōrmās trānsferendus est
phrases.english: and as soon as the milk has set, it is to be moved into baskets, wicker trays, or moulds

phrases.latin: In lactis duōs congiōs addunt coāgulum magnitūdine oleae, ut coeat
phrases.english: To two gallons of milk they add rennet the size of an olive, to make it set

sources: Lewis & Short: concresco · Lewis & Short: coeo
